title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC1RA_---1LD_1LE0RA_1LF0LE_0RB0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC1RA_---1LD_1LE0RA_1LF0LE_0RB0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At each visit of the right end the tape is a block of 10111010 words that grows, then a region transformed by a fixed map, with a chaotic counter next to the block eating a reservoir. Three events so far (after sweeps 24, 91 and 9,305) each turned the block into a new reservoir; the third, which earlier notes left unexplained, is confirmed on the true run. The present region has 18,659 cells and should last about 21100 sweeps. No scaled-down model of this machine was seen to halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 48,970 cells have been visited and 29,203 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The sweep map ignores the block; three events
claims.text: At each visit of the right end in state B the tape, read leftwards, is B>0 (10111010)^n R. With the block cut to 10 words at every visit, R agrees with the true run at all of the first 8,000 visits. On the true run R jumps after visits 24 (31 to 71 cells), 91 (77 to 213) and 9,305 (229 to 18,659), without a halt.

claims.title: No halt in 4·10<sup>6</sup> sweeps after the third event
claims.text: From the true configuration at visit 9,320 the shortened run makes 4·10<sup>6</sup> visits without a halt or an event.

claims.title: Next event about 2<sup>1100</sup> sweeps away
claims.text: The counter's front advances about 16.6 cells per doubling of the number of sweeps; the reservoir has about 18,400 cells.

claims.title: No scaled-down version halts
claims.text: With the block cut to 2, 3 or 5 words at every visit from the start, there is no halt in 5·10<sup>6</sup> visits.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: The head sweeps across the whole tape and adds a word per sweep at the right end, so the tape grows like the square root of the step count.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The halting pattern 0 B>0 has not been excluded at the far end, and no invariant of the tail left by an event is known.

check: ./rvis 1RB1RD_1LC1RA_---1LD_1LE0RA_1LF0LE_0RB0LB R B - 10111010 100000 1 1 9400 0 | awk '{d=$4-p; if(d>20||d<-20) print; p=$4}'   # events on the true run

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A block of repeated eight-cell words grows at every sweep; behind it a scrambled counter slowly eats a reservoir, and when the reservoir is gone the whole block becomes the next one. This page runs the real machine in your browser and explains the pieces.

facts.text: The region behind the block since the third event (sweep 9,305).
After sweeps 24, 91 and 9,305, all seen on the true run, none of them a halt.
Estimated wait for the next event.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A growing block, a busy counter, a reservoir
html: This machine grows to the right. Look at the tape each time the head reaches the right end and read it leftwards: first a block of copies of the word 10111010, one more than last time; then a short busy stretch that changes from sweep to sweep; then a long regular reservoir; and a short old tail at the fixed end. (The picture shows the mirror image.)

<svg viewBox="0 0 580 70" role="img" aria-label="The tape: a growing uniform block, an active counter region, a reservoir it eats, and an old tail at the far end" style="width:100%;max-width:620px;height:auto"><g font-family="var(--body)" font-size="11" fill="var(--fg2)"><text x="10" y="14">← grows one word a sweep</text><text x="14" y="60">growing block</text><text x="184" y="60">busy counter</text><text x="274" y="60">reservoir</text><text x="484" y="60">old tail</text></g><rect x="10" y="20" width="170" height="22" fill="var(--ink)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="180" y="20" width="90" height="22" fill="var(--heur-bg)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="270" y="20" width="210" height="22" fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="480" y="20" width="90" height="22" fill="var(--sunk)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/></svg>

Crossing the block changes nothing: the machine applies one fixed rule to the region behind the block, sweep after sweep. There is a rhythm of four sweeps: the head goes 7 cells into the region, then 1, then 7, and on the fourth sweep some varying distance.

sections.heading: A counter that eats its reservoir, then refills it
html: The busy stretch behaves like a scrambled odometer: cells next to the block change all the time, deeper ones more and more rarely, and the deepest cell ever touched advances about 17 cells each time the number of sweeps doubles.

When it reaches the far end there is an event: the whole block is turned into a fresh reservoir and a new block starts. Events so far: after sweeps 24, 91 and 9,305. The third made the region 18,659 cells long, which should last about 21100 sweeps.

sections.heading: A coin toss, repeated at ever longer intervals
html: Between two events nothing can go wrong: the machine sweeps, the block grows, the counter eats a little more reservoir. Everything is decided in the few sweeps in which the counter touches the far end of the tape. Each such contact either stops the machine or turns the block into the next reservoir, which is as long as the block had become, so the next contact is exponentially further away than the last one, and the one after that exponentially further again.

<svg viewBox="0 0 580 96" role="img" aria-label="Epochs: each reservoir is as long as the block was at the previous event, so each epoch is exponentially longer than the one before" style="width:100%;max-width:620px;height:auto"><g font-family="var(--body)" font-size="11" fill="var(--fg2)"><text x="10" y="14">epoch k: reservoir of L cells</text><text x="10" y="58">epoch k+1: reservoir of about 2^(L/c) cells</text><text x="300" y="36">eaten in about 2^(L/c) sweeps</text></g><rect x="10" y="20" width="60" height="18" fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="70" y="20" width="14" height="18" fill="var(--sunk)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="10" y="64" width="520" height="18" fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="530" y="64" width="14" height="18" fill="var(--sunk)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><circle cx="84" cy="29" r="4" fill="var(--head)"/><circle cx="544" cy="73" r="4" fill="var(--head)"/></svg>

Machines like this are called cryptids in the Busy Beaver community: their fate hangs on an unbounded sequence of yes/no questions about a pseudo-random process, and no known method answers all of them at once.

The machine halts only if state B arrives on a 0 with another 0 just behind it. Unlike for its sister machines, no scaled-down version of this one was seen to halt, so it is not even clear which way to bet: it may be that the far end never offers the fatal pattern, but nobody has found the reason.

sections.heading: What was checked, and how
html:
• A version of the machine that cuts the block back to 10 words at every sweep sees exactly the same region as the real machine at each of the first 8,000 sweeps.
  • The real machine was run through the third event; from there the shortened version runs 4 million more sweeps without a halt.
  • Not known: the counter's rule, and any invariant of the far end.

family: chaotic counter eating a reservoir (mirror image, 8-cell words; cryptid-like)
summary: Mirror image of the reservoir counters: a block of 10111010 words grows at the right and a chaotic counter eats a reservoir (about 17 cells per doubling of sweeps); events after sweeps 24, 91 and 9,305 (region now 18,659 cells), the next about 2^1100 sweeps away.
